exceptions.what: block-metadata.ts:240 `"anchor"` -> `""` in anchorLineShape's ternary
exceptions.reason: RETIRED by issue #46 shape 2, and the twin of the list-hazard.ts:67 row below is reworded with it. The old classification was UNREACHABLE, on the argument that the ternary is reached only for a PARAGRAPH whose sole child is an inline anchor and that such a paragraph exists only where the source line FAILED the block-anchor grammar - a line that passes being held back as a `blockAnchor` node that returned before the ternary. Both halves of that argument are now false. The record counts out the children the PRINTER emits nothing for, so a line whose tail is in the packer's word split but NOT in the reader's rstrip set (a no-break space, a thin space, an ideographic space, a byte-order mark - issue #67's set) stays a paragraph the reader refused and reaches the output as a live anchor; and the `blockAnchor` arm no longer short-circuits, so every valid anchor line reaches the ternary too. The `"anchor"` answer is now taken by tests at both levels: `tests/parser/block-attributes.test.ts` asserts it for `[[anc]]` plus each of those four tails and for the whole anchor-spelling table, and `tests/format/block-attributes.test.ts` pins the byte/idempotence pair. STALE MEASUREMENT, kept for the record: 0 paragraphs answering `"anchor"` against 83,644 answering `"lookalike"`, over 319,216 documents (the depth-5 list-shape sweep, a depth-5 product over `* a`, `[[anc]]`, `[[id,]]`, `[[id, ]]`, `[[3-bad]]`, `[[3-bad,Ref]]`, `[[9]]`, `para`, `+`, blank and `[role]`, and a depth-4 inline-mark product). That count predates this change, and its generator carries no exotic whitespace, so it measured a population the new shape is not in. The row is classified `now` because the mutant should already be killed; it stays until a cleared-cache mutation run says so, and that run removes it.

exceptions.what: list-hazard.ts:115 `!transparent` -> `true`, so the run keeps the line comments it reads through
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT. `run` has exactly two readers, `run.length === 0` and `run.some(blockTitle)`, and a line comment is no block title - so the two spellings can differ only for a leading adjacent run made of comments ALONE. That run cannot exist: a `//` line becomes a BLOCK of the item only once something else has already ended the item's text (until then `skip_line_comments` reads it through and the line after it continues the text), and that something is a block standing in front of the comment. Measured: 0 comments-only leading runs over 259,729 list items in the same 319,216 documents

exceptions.what: list.ts:139 `if (item.detachedTail) return false;` -> the guard never fires (#56's new code)
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT: the loop under the guard returns false at its very first block anyway. `detachedTail` is set only when the item's LAST block is a frozen `+` paragraph (list-item-node.ts's endsInPlusParagraph), such a paragraph is neither an indented literal nor a list, and its printed gap is never empty: the frozen `+` is by construction the SECOND `+` of an adjacent run, and the first one is the erased cell the gap record spells as `+`. So the reversed walk falls straight to `printedGap(...).length > 0` and returns false, which is what the guard returns. printedGap can only empty a gap for a nested LIST sharing its parent's marker, which this block is not. Measured: over the 111,110 depth-5 sweep documents a detachedTail item carries exactly ONE block signature, a `paragraph` behind the gap `["+"]`, and an instrumented build that computes both answers logs zero disagreements

exceptions.what: list.ts:84 `block.type === "delimitedBlock"` -> `true`

exceptions.what: the default arm of the node dispatch (printer.ts:146-153) — 4 NoCoverage mutants
exceptions.reason: an EQUIVALENT arm forced by the type system: Prettier's AstPath is invariant, so the printer's node union must admit the inline nodes a paragraph's children array is typed with. Every block that owns inline content builds its atoms itself, so no path reaches this arm; deleting it is a type error

exceptions.what: reflow.ts:234 `/\s+/v` -> `/\s/v` in splitWords
exceptions.reason: The only difference between the two splits is the empty strings a single-character split emits between adjacent whitespace, and `.filter((word) => word.length > 0)` erases exactly those. The two produce the same array for every input

exceptions.what: reflow.ts:365 `last < 0` -> `false` in escapeDanglingPlus
exceptions.reason: Dead by the caller contract: `endNodeAtoms` is the only caller and has already returned when `last < 0`, so the guard re-checks a state it can never be in. Killing it needs a direct call with an empty atom list — a test-only construction of unreachable state

exceptions.what: reflow.ts:515 `let glueNext = false` -> `true` in wordsToAtoms
exceptions.reason: The initializer is read only on the first iteration, and there `fuseBackwards = index > 0 && (glueNext || …)` short-circuits on `index > 0` before `glueNext` is looked at. Every later read sees the value the previous iteration assigned

exceptions.what: keepContinuationLine's two entry guards (reflow.ts:411 `atoms.length === 0` -> `false`, reflow.ts:412 `atoms[0].text !== CONTINUATION_WORD` -> `false`)
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT by the caller's contract. `opensWithOne` is `opensWithContinuationLine(node)` (src/print/inline.ts), which is true only when the node starts at column 1 and its value STARTS with `"+\n"` - so the word list is non-empty and its first word is exactly `+`, which is what the two guards re-check. The same fact is why the caller can push `atoms[0]` unconditionally one line later. Measured: 36,960 nodes the printer reads as continuation openers over 319,216 documents, 0 of them with a first word other than `+`

exceptions.what: reflow.ts:418 `breakBefore: "hard"` -> `""` in keepContinuationLine
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT: `wrap` reads the field exactly twice, once as `!== "none"` (is there a forced break) and once as `=== "literal"` (does the line start at column 0 instead of the continuation indent). `""` answers both questions the way `"hard"` does, so only the `"literal"` spelling is distinguishable at all

exceptions.what: narrow()'s guard and message — the uncovered half of the file
exceptions.reason: narrow's throw is the assertion-failure path of a test helper: it fires only when a test asserted the wrong node type, so a passing suite never covers it, and killing its mutants means writing a deliberately failing assertion

exceptions.what: contentOpensAfterBreak's narrowing guard (block-start-hazard.ts:107 `!("children" in node)` -> `false`, and the `return false` it guards -> `true`, the file's only NoCoverage row)
exceptions.reason: TYPE-FORCED. `hazardAtBlockStart` asks `contentOpensAfterBreak(cursor.siblings[0])` only behind `cursor.index === 0`, so the node handed over IS the span the question is about, and a span always has `children`. The guard is the narrow TypeScript demands before `children` can be read off an `InlineNode` at all; deleting it is a type error

exceptions.what: the two `X.type === "text"` guards (block-start-hazard.ts:109 in contentOpensAfterBreak, :183 in opensWithSourceBreak) - 2 mutants, each -> `true`
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT. Dropping either guard leaves its regex to read `.value`, and among inline nodes only `text` and `rawLine` carry one: a rawLine holds ONE source line, so its value has no `\n` and neither pattern can match, and every other node yields `undefined`, which the test coerces to the string `"undefined"`. exceptions.what: block-start-hazard.ts:164 `breakBefore: "literal"` -> `""`, and block-start-hazard.ts:158 `second.breakBefore !== "none"` -> `false` (2 mutants)
exceptions.reason: EQUIVALENT, both for the indent. `wrap` distinguishes `"none"` from everything else, and then `"literal"` from everything else only to pick the line's indent (`lineIndent = run.breakBefore === "literal" ? 0 : indent`). The net runs only where `blockAtColumnZero` holds, which is the printer's paragraph and standalone-inline arms, and both call `blockBody(..., 0)` - so the indent the other spelling selects is 0, the number `"literal"` names. The `!== "none"` guard is the same fact from the other side: past it the atom already carries a forced break with no fuse flag set, so the write can change only the break's KIND

EQUIVALENT under the reader's own normalization. `Helpers.prepare_source_string` rstrips every line, so no source line ends in horizontal whitespace and the `[^\S\n]*` run both patterns allow is always EMPTY; and a paragraph's first line cannot begin with whitespace (leading whitespace makes it a literal paragraph), so the `\s*` the second pattern opens with is empty too. With both runs empty every spelling accepts and rejects the same strings

The mutant fires the net for a span whose content opens with a horizontal SPACE and holds a break further along. Reaching it needs the composed atom to be block syntax at line start, which for the four span marks means the `#` spelling: `* b` and `** b` on a block's first line are read as a LIST, so there is no paragraph left to guard. The one witness is `## b
c## d

` - a document whose rendering already diverges, because the classifier reads a paragraph where the oracle reads a heading. Pinning it would pin that divergence. TRIGGER - issue #63; the row belongs to the commit that teaches the classifier the Markdown heading spelling
